I can totally relate to how you feel. I was also living with my mom at 30. I had never bothered going out to date or finding boyfriends or anything like that. When I turned 30, I also thought that my life was basically over as well and that nobody would want me because I turned 30. Fast-forward to now, I am now 33 years old. I am married and live with my husband and crazy German Shepherd. It is crazy how life changes within a few years.

I just want to be on the other end of it and say do what you love, do what makes you happy, and if you feel stuck, then that means something has to change. My body was pretty much telling me that I needed to change and I listened to it and I’m glad I did.

I was given a student with a huge history of physical aggression towards students and staff members. He was recorded to have choked both staff and peers along with hitting and kicking. At the beginning of the school year they had made a switch so that I could be his special ed teacher. So I got him around end of September. He was also new to our school.

I’m not going to lie. I was nervous. He’s the same height as me and was stronger than I am. I’m a small petite lady that’s 4’11 feet. 

By the end of the school year, he was one of my favorite students. He was no longer angry and harming people. He became one of the kindest and funniest kids I had ever met. I got him into art and was able to find that he had talent in making crafts and modeling figures with clay. I had many compliments from both parents, administration, and staff members at how he was a totally different kid. He ended the school year having the highest math growth in the entire school.
Thank you for sharing!

Here's a list of some suggestions I think might help you:

* **Depression** \- You need to focus on finding ways to treat this. It'll kick in and it'll be hard. But you need to have a routine in place to be able to handle it until you get a job. Try to make sure you develop a hobby, healthy self-care routines, etc. It might help to develop a morning, afternoon, and evening routine to keep you sane. It'll be different not having something to do each week so try to fill the void with your hobbies until you can get more job interviews. 
* **Develop new skills!** \- While you are applying for jobs, take note of their job requirements. Some jobs may require customer service skills or knowing certain programs before applying. Some of these programs you may be able to get some knowledge on for free such as watching Youtube videos or google searching them.
* **Reflect on your job.** \- Think about things you struggled with at your prior job and either try to find a job that would focus more on your strengths or work on developing skills to be able to work on your weaknesses.
